title: An Old Dream Left
subtitle: I often think of that place, with the lake water seeping through the cabin and the desk lamp calmly strolling amid cobwebs and beams.

items.text: To Winnifred
An Old Dream Left
My name is Brian Finn.
A ... less than accomplished film director.
With the meager talents given to me by God, I've made films that defy classification as either good or bad.
Yet, I've never managed to create a film I can truly call my own.
Now, even the generosity of the divine has reached its end.
Bedroom

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: *cough*
His rough hand trembles as it gropes around.
It runs over the table's edge, brushes past a half-open medicine box, knocks over an uncapped pen, but never reaches its intended destination.

items.speaker: Illia
items.text: Dad, stop looking through those old film reels. Dr. David said you should be resting in bed!

items.speaker: Illia
items.text: Besides, your work's already won over all those investors, and they're sharper than Wall Street's finest.

items.speaker: Illia
items.text: What regrets could you possibly have left?
Her brother speaks up, his pride in his father's achievements ringing in his voice.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: Yeah, Dad, the critics have nothing but praise for your movies, especially New England Dream!
The old man's hand lingers in the air.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: No, my dear boy. New England Dream is the biggest regret of my life.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Forty years squandered on that thing, and I still never truly completed it.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: The editing alone took up years of my life.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: But no matter how many changes I made, I couldn't fill that emptiness. That failure has haunted me for decades. To this very day, in fact.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: At this point, I have no choice but to confess that I failed to capture the essence of a true vampire.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Not even ... Not even a sliver of that elusive inspiration.
The old man becomes agitated, sparking a coughing fit.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Compared to the vampire I saw, it lacks something vital, some essential element.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: But what could that be, Dad?

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: *cough* I ... I don't know.
A hushed silence falls in the bedroom. Even the sound of Brian's hurried breaths is fading.
They are becoming slow and intermittent, as if they might cease at any moment.
A profound regret weighs heavily upon each breath.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Son, would you get me my notebook from the desk?

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Yes, and turn it to the latest page.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: Yes, Dad. I'll get it right away.
The boy hastens out the door, while the girl looks at her father with a melancholy gaze, her face etched with concern.

items.speaker: Illia
items.text: But your eyes ...

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Heh. Don't worry about me, Illia.
His eyes have long lost their vitality. They are embedded in deep, wrinkled sockets.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: It's been my faithful companion for many years. Even with these failing eyes of mine, I can still read the thing through touch alone.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: Dad, here. Here it is.
Robin carefully places the notebook in his father's hand.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Ah, yes, this is far more useful than any concoction of pills. Don't you agree, old friend?
With some effort, he steadies his frail frame.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I still need you to document everything faithfully. At least for now, anyway.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: We have one last journey to make—the final stretch.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: *cough" Now, where should I begin?

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: This tale begins in New England, I believe.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Back then, I was young, timid, and filled with fear of the unknown.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Until ...
1930s, New England
A cabin, nestled between dense woods and a lake. A common sight in any horror film.
Moss climbs the windowsills and eaves of the cabin's exterior, as if silently repelling any visitors.
Sadly, it does nothing to repel young, reckless children.

items.speaker: Tom
items.text: D**n! You reckon there's really a witch here brewing potions from baby hair?

items.speaker: Jared
items.text: Haha! What kind of baloney are you talking about now?

items.speaker: Jared
items.text: I heard there's a vampire hanging around in these woods. You know, the kind that has fangs with hollow tips so it can pierce the skin on your neck and suck your blood.
He places his hand on the quivering shoulder beside him.

items.speaker: Jared
items.text: Good grief! Would you look at our Little Brian? If he shivered any faster, he could be a hand-crank operator at my uncle's generator factory!

items.speaker: Tom
items.text: I bet he's already got a fresh diaper at the ready!

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: C-Cut it out, guys.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: We should head back. I really don't want to fall behind on Mrs. Madison's homework.
Jared pats him on the shoulder and pushes him forward.

items.speaker: Jared
items.text: Don't worry, Little Brian. Legend has it that the vampire's keen on blood from strapping young men, not scrawny little monkeys!

items.speaker: Tom
items.text: Hah. Then Brian will be the safest one among us!
The pressure on Brian's shoulder intensifies.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: That l-legend's probably a bunch of hooey, right?

items.speaker: Tom
items.text: Hahaha! Of course it is!

items.speaker: Jared
items.text: Yeah, so what are you so afraid of, Little Brian?
A breeze blows past the door, causing it to creak creepily.

items.speaker: Tom
items.text: Off you go, good sir! Take a gander deeper inside for us and say, "How do you do?" to Mr. Vampire!
The shove from behind sends Brian staggering forward.
He falls into an even more sinister-looking room, hitting his head on the corner of a table.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Ahh!

items.speaker: Tom
items.text: Oh, look what you've done now, you klutz! You've scared off all the critters!

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Ouch ... My head ...

items.speaker: Jared
items.text: Bye-bye, Little Brian. We'll be waiting for your triumphant return to town.
The door slams shut.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Don't leave me here! You can't do this to me. I don't want to be eaten by a vampire!
His head spins as his consciousness slips away into darkness.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Ugh ...
A loud, rumbling sound approaches from afar.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: That noise ... It feels like my head's about to explode. Good lord, is that an earthquake?!
Blue.
A subtle blue seeps into the room.
From under the bed. Through the cracks in the wooden floor.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: You are ...?

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Am I hallucinating? Or is this ...

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Is there really a vampire living here?!
Blue ripples wash over the walls. The desk, the lamp, and the wooden chair are all tinged with its cool hue.
They pick themselves up and start moving. They dance in the endless blue, eventually surrounding the young boy.
It is as if they have been brought to life.
Hm?
You don't look too well, my uninvited friend.
Need a hand?

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I-I ... um ... y-you ...

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Are you a vampire?
The angel-faced woman seems uninclined to answer.
Hah! Clearly, you're in desperate need of a good rest.
The blue has reached his temples, blanketing everything in sight.
He gives in, sinking into slumber and returning to tranquility.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I've never forgotten what I saw that day.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I firmly believe that in that cramped little cabin, I saw a true vampire.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: She was so beautiful, so captivating, and brimming with a passion for life.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: That was our first encounter.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: After that, I fantasized countless times about meeting her again.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Until ...

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Back then, I was young, timid, and filled with fear of the unknown.
TO BE CONTINUED…
